[Predictions]

Lookboonmee vs. Amorim
Lookboonmee, DEC
I might switch on this because it's a 50-50 fight, but as an early prediction, I've got to go with Loma. The big reach advantage for Amorim is worrisome because Loma's going to look to strike, and I worry about her getting those body kicks caught and getting dumped on the mat over and over again. Loma was taken down repeatedly by Loopy Godinez and Alexia Thainara, and if they can get takedowns, then Amorim can, too. Loopy also succeeded at making Lookbonmee fade by R2 from the grappling pressure, but Amorim is a fader herself. She’s only ever won in the later rounds against Monsterrat Ruiz, who is not good at all and certainly not on the same level as Loma. Loma has shown a much better ability of succeeding in the later rounds than Amorim, so, basically, this has to be Lookbonmee by DEC or Amorim SUB R1, maybe R2. The question then is, which option is more likely? Thainara is no slouch with the submissions herself and hunted for several against Loma but came up short. Amorim is a better pure BJJ player than Thainara, but in terms of MMA, I rate Thainara much higher than Amorim. So, if Thainara couldn't find the sub, that's a little bit reassuring for us Lookboonmee enjoyers. This might be a casual take, but I see a bit of Ronda Rousey in Amorim. It’s early submission or bust. In that fight against Inoue where Amorim went in as a big favorite, she faded really badly in R2 and looked sloppy as hell on the feet. Loma’s not the best when it comes to TDD or getting back to her feet, but she can do it competently, although she tends to cede significant control time, and I do worry that she'll be too willing to mess around on the mat. On the feet, I don’t think it’s going to be close. Loma might not be Weili Zhang, but she’s got good muay thai, and I could see her hurting Amorim with the knees and elbows if there’s more than a few minutes of striking. I’m dreading the possibility of Amorim looking like a -1000 favorite by getting an easy takedown and armbar in the first round, but I think Loma can survive R1, defend takedowns later, and get the 29-28.

posts.author: AyyLmaonnaise
posts.content:
[Predictions]

Aoriqileng vs Haddon
Haddon SUB RD 1

Man, I've been waiting so long for another Haddon fight. He was one of the best guys from his season of DWCS (imo) and had to pull out of two fights that would’ve massively boosted his profile (he would’ve won both imo). It’s a real shame he’s picked up all these injuries because he is on the later side of his 20s and missed out on an entire year of activity. UFC punished him by not letting him fight in Perth but they are giving him a layup here. I’ve always been a fan of AQ but he has just never panned out. That last win was incredibly shocking and honestly his best performance ever, but it was also a 30 second bonk against a guy who is now 3-8 in the ufc. AQ has always had power and I’ve been a fan of his boxing in the pocket, but he is a very limited, very low level fighter who hasn’t improved much. All AQ does is brawl, when he isn’t standing in the pocket throwing he is staring at you at range, absorbing shots. He is good in the pocket but even then his game is limited, as he headhunts and is extremely hittable. Haddon is going to brawl with him so this is somewhat favorable, but Haddon is way more skilled and possesses a deep bag of tricks at his display. The only way I see AQ winning this fight is by another bonk like last fight. Haddon does get hit a lot with his style but he keeps a tight guard and seems pretty durable (you have to be when you fight like he does). I think his boxing is way above AQ’s: his hands are faster, he has way more output, and he attacks the body frequently. AQ has no real form of defense and with Haddon’s insane pace I see AQ getting absolutely swamped with volume. AQ can fight at a frantic pace too but he does not have good cardio at all, slowly down heavily at the halfway mark; sometimes earlier if he’s really getting his **** kicked in. Haddon did get tired in his debut but anyone would’ve at that pace; even then he still fight hard to the end and won every round. There’s a stark difference between getting tired and knowing how to fight through it, versus gassing and falling apart; Haddon is the former and AQ the latter. When AQ gets tired his already bad defense becomes nonexistent, and he just swings with reckless abandon. I expect him to slow heavily because of Haddon’s pace, especially with the body work mixed in. Haddon also has a wrestling background and is not afraid to mix in takedowns of his own, which should pay dividends here. AQ has okay first layer tdd but he is a very bad grappler and does nothing once grounded. Even in fights he dominated like the Munoz one, AQ still found ways to get slowed down with grappling. A td threat also massively slows down his offense, as he becomes far too cautious of getting taken down. A prime example of this is the Rosas fight, Rosas was gassed and doing nothing on the feet, and AQ refused to push the action & resigned to losing a 29-28. I don’t think he will stop throwing because Haddon is going to force him into a war, but if he does mix in takedowns I think he is going to break AQ quickly. I was going to pick KO initially since AQ turns into a punching bag very quickly and has been dropped many times, but I kind of think we see a club and sub like DWCS. The reason AQ isn’t getting slept every fight despite these red flags is because he is insanely tough; you have to KO him cold in order to get him out of there. I think Haddon is going to overwhelm him with strikes and hurt him a lot, but since he is an attritional volume guy, I think he will either mix in takedowns or drop AQ, and then go for the RNC. Haddon has a very sneaky back take and once he softens AQ up I think he is going to go for the finish. Regardless of the result I expect a Haddon finish here; the way he fights, it is going to be really rough for AQ to see a decision.

Tsuruya vs Gurule
Tsuruya DEC

Quite funny to see Gurule back so quickly after his last one; I’m almost positive the UFC told him he had to take this fight for a contract extension. This is a harder matchup for Rei but not because Gurule is good, I simply thought Aguilar was a complete layup style for him. Aguilar is a midget who doesn’t defend takedowns and has lost to every grappler he's faced. Gurule is much more complete and 100% has better tdd than Aguilar, but the problem with him is that he is mid at everything. I said it last week and I’ll say it again, he is simply just a nothingburger, all he does in the cage is go through the motions. He finally had a performance where he actually did something, and even then it was underwhelming; he just may be the weakest puncher in all of UFC. I don’t get how you can land 70+ strikes on someone in a round and not even score so much as a knockdown. The volume looks insane on paper but if you watch the fight back, outside of flurries all he was doing was throwing a singular strike every few seconds, which contributed to output. He’s definitely a better striker than Rei but idk how much he will get to use it here. One thing that makes this tricky is Gurule’s get ups are actually really solid; every time he gets taken down he scrambles up to his feet very quickly. He did very well against a D1 wrestler on DWCS, but Nick P also has no bjj to complement his takedowns, thus allowing Gurule to get up with no resistance. I do expect Gurule to get up a bunch, but I doubt he can stop the successive attack. Rei is a really good chain wrestler and his attack on top is definitely not something Gurule has fought before. In fact, there really isn’t a ton of footage of Gurule on bottom, so idk how he will fair if Rei gets him there; I definitely know he won’t be able to pop up as effortlessly as dwcs. If this stays standing obviously I expect Gurule to win but since he has 0 danger factor it may just allow Rei to shoot and get him down. My main worry with Rei here is cardio; his cardio is simply just bad. He’s lost every 3rd round he’s been in and badly at that: cruising for 4+ min on his back against Hernandez, dropped by Climaco, Van fight. However, this fight is at 135 due to the short notice and that should help Rei. Personally I don’t think he will ever fix his cardio at 125 because he has a massive weight cut, but at 135 I expect it to be better. Even though I'm sure he’s walking around close to 135, b2b weight cuts and 20+ hour fights cannot be beneficial for  Gurule. While a clean win, that was anything but a performance he left unscathed; that was a 3 round war, it’s not like he slept Barez in 30 seconds and called it a day. Gurule’s best weapon is his cardio but I am curious if he can push the same pace he always does. I see this as an almost identical matchup to Rei vs Hernandez; he’s fighting a guy with skills everywhere but doesn’t excel in any one area, and also has next to no threat of knocking Rei out. I’m tempted to pick Sub since I have a feeling that this grinding, wrestling heavy style could really wear on Gurule, but at the same time Rei hasn’t really come close to any sort of sub on anyone with a pulse, so I will go decision.

Hill vs Xiong
Xiong DEC

I’m really glad the UFC signed Xiong. She won’t be around for long due to her age but she is a skilled fighter and was pretty fun to watch in ONE. The Hill test is always a good measure of skill so we should learn a lot here. If this was taking place with the Meng Bo fight excluded, I would say Xiong is a lock here. She looked good on tape and the decline of Hill has been well documented. Her tape prior to that fight was very impressive, she was dominating pretty much all of her fights and her only loss in ONE was a fight I thought she was cruising in before a wild 5th round comeback from Lee. After beating Lee in the trilogy, the crooks at ONE sidelined her for 3 years. She came back against Meng Bo and robbed her pretty badly; she won due to ONE’s weird scoring system but if this was anywhere else she would’ve dropped a clear 29-28 loss. This fight is making things confusing for me, it wasn’t like Bo did anything crazy, it was more so Xiong could not get going until r3; for the first 10 minutes she got cage pushed, wouldn’t throw anything on the feet, and just allowed Bo to grind on her. She finally woke up in r3, countering a throw and taking the back, easily controlling the round and winning it with little effort. Being 38 and having the long career she’s had, I am pretty worried that she may be washed. She got sidelined for 3 years and looked very off compared to her older fights. I do think ring rust played a huge role here though, as she easily won r3 once she actually started doing something. To me it wasn’t like Bo was outskilling her, Xiong just literally could not get anything going. Seeing her be the large favorite that she is, is pretty scary, but at the same time now that she is back in the game maybe she looks better. Age is definitely a concern but athleticism falls off much later for women than it does men; you can still be in your late 30s and keep kicking it at a high level. I think it;s also worth noting that was her first fight in a ring as well, which would probably explain her issues getting away from the clinch. She did show that she struggles getting held there in the Lee fights too, so this could be a path for Hill. However Hill is not a grappler nor is she ever grappling heavy; only doing it a handful of times. Even if she does come out wrestling, I don’t think she’s that good at it to neutralize Xiong. She could get stalled in the clinch again but I will cut her some slack for that Bo fight. Even then, her get ups are good and she’s honestly pretty difficult to take down. In a striking match, I think Xiong should take this. Hill is always high output and a great vet but she has been looking really bad lately. Her athleticism is finally starting to fall off, she’s reacting really badly to strikes, she moves very slow, and her cardio weirdly isn’t looking that good either. She’s still got skills but she’s been looking really bad on the feet lately; I also thought she lost to Souza so you could argue she’s dropped her last 4. The Ricci fight was most concerning to me because Ricci is one of the most useless strikers in the division and while close, she still outhustled Hill. Xiong has a funky striking style but I really like it. Barring the Bo fight, Xiong’s hands look really crisp and she goes for it in all her fights. She isn’t much of a KO artist but she does throw everything pretty hard. I really like her straight right and she does a great job of throwing her hooks at weird angles, making them hard to predict. She also has some nasty body kicks, which could go a long way here since Hill’s cardio/pace is not what it used to be. In her other fights, Xiong also moves around a lot, both with her feet and her hands. She is never in one place and is always switching stances & throwing out different feints. I don’t feel very good about this pick simply because of Xiong’s last fight; I do think ring rust played a factor but with her age and layoff it does raise a lot of concerns. As valid as those concerns are though, Hill is very clearly washed and this could be one of if not her last fight. She has lost her pace and cardio edge, which was her biggest strength, her athleticism is declining too; I think she has looked a career worst in terms of speed these last few fights. I doubt she gets chinned but her durability hasn’t been looking great either. Not like she’s getting dropped or finished, but she is reacting really badly every time she gets hit now. I don’t think Xiong is going to KO her but she throws pretty hard and throws everything with precision so maybe she could be the one to do it; I just really don’t like Hill’s reactions to getting hit, she looks like she wants out with every clean strike landed. In hindsight this could end up being one of the most obvious Hill upsets ever against someone who is washed, but I will give Xiong the benefit of the doubt and assume she shows up better than her last one. Even if she doesn’t, as long as it’s a competitive fight there’s always the chance that Hill gets robbed, especially fighting a Chinese in “home” territory.

Zhu vs Vera
Zhu DEC

On paper this looks like an amazing fight, both guys have really flashy records and look really good at face value. However, these guys ******* SUCK. I’ve taped curtain jerker WMMA fighters more exciting than these two. Not only are they bad watches, they aren’t even good fighters either. Both of these guys are literal nothingburgers who do the bare minimum to win. I liked Zhu a lot taping him for RTU, and he looked amazing in the opening round against Ando. After that fight though, he’s looked like ****. Zhu is kind of your classic Chinese NPC fighter; he has a flashy record but does barely anything to win fights. I will cut him some slack for the Bin/Haraguchi fights, as the former was his good friend and training partner and the latter a td spammer who gave him 0 space to separate. Despite those outside influences, he’s just not impressive. Zhu does have a ton of power but he doesn’t fight very aggressive and is honestly a pretty bad finisher; he has to one tap you or else he’s just gonna sit back at range and throw nothing. His tdd is actually pretty good and he stands up quickly, but guys who constantly force him to defend (like Ando/Shin) cause him to get stuck against the cage playing defense and limit his alrady very low output. I don’t think Zhu is a bad fighter per se, but he is just an exister to me. I get why he’s the underdog as he arguably lost to Bin and is an NPC, but Vera ******* sucks. He looks amazing on paper and even has good wins to legitimize his record, but then you watch his fights and it tells a whole other story; Vera is legitimately one of the most boring fighters I’ve ever watched. He’s like Colby Thicknesse but with better striking, all he does is win on these thin margin fights and does the bare minimum to win. I really don’t think he’s that skilled either; yes, he is beating good comp but he hardly beats them impressively. His only loss for example came to Torres, and he lost because all he did was cage push. Torres didn’t do anything flashy, all he did was fight behind kicks and his jab. On the feet Vera throws absolutely nothing, doesn’t use any of his tools, and has no power either. These guys are both very low volume and don’t separate well but at least Zhu has power which can make a difference. I’ve seen him get some vicious ko’s on the regional scene and he’s dropped a lot of people even if he doesn’t get a finish. I think both of these guys are gonna do more feinting than throwing actual shots, but I give a slight lean to Zhu simply because he has actual power; I really don’t think Vera can beat many UFC fighters on the feet. Not even because I think he’s bad, but he simply just doesn’t do anything; like, even less so than Zhu, who is already insanely low volume as it is. Vera is going to wrestle here which I don’t like. Zhu already faced a much better wrestler in Shin, and while ugly he made it very difficult for Shin to establish top control, only getting held down for a few seconds at a time. The caveat is that his volume did suffer massively as a resukt. However while Vera forces wrestling, I simply don’t think it’s that good. He doesn’t chain wrestle well and as a result he just ends up cage pushing 90% of the time. He has no wrestling background and doesn’t have any advanced methods to get the fight down, just a basic understanding. His control has looked pretty mid as well and like the rest of his game, he never looks to do any form of damage. The only guys he’s had a ton of success grounding is bums like Zenidim. I think Zhu’s tdd is definitely not great but seeing him pop up to his feet with relative ease against Shin/Ando makes me think he should be okay here. I know the Chinese scene is a mixed bag but it’s hard to trust South American wrestling as well. Plus you have to factor in that Vera is flying across the world as the B side, and is also not a natural FW; he was going to be on TUF at 135 so he isn’t cutting much weight at all. I think this line is a bit wiki capped, I don’t think either are good but Vera being a fav just feels wrong to me; that 21-1-1 record is extremely deceptive. I think this is going to be a ******* horrible fight and a very greasy split decision. I don’t have a lot of confidence in Zhu but imo he is the better fighter here; I am seriously unimpressed with Vera. Zhu is either going to need to massively **** the bed (entirely possible) or Vera magically level up his game in the last few months to justify this price imo. If you’re staying up to watch this card, take a nap for this fight; I can guarantee its going to be ******* awful unless Zhu gets a random bonk.

Lookboonme vs Amorim
Amorim SUB RD 2

This is a very difficult fight to call right off the bat. UFC is doing their usual sink-or-swim matchmaking with a prospect they like; Amorim is coming off of a really embarrassing loss to Mizuki where she looked exactly like her old self, now the ufc is giving her an (arguably) more accomplished and experienced girl who was just in top 15 last fight. Stylistically this is a pretty good matchup for Amorim but I’m really not sure if it’s as black and white as it seems. Loma has servicable grappling but her tdd is not good and once on her back she is pretty useless. She’s not as bad as say when she fought Angela Hill, but being 30 and getting mauled like she did last fight, I’m not really expecting much improvements. Loma kind of seems like a no brainer just looking at this on paper; she’s fought significantly better comp, has good enough tdd, the better striker by an extreme margin, and she’s just more proven overall. However, I have a bad feeling about the grappling here. For all her flaws Amorim is still a very high level grappler. I absolutely hate how she fights like its a BJJ match, but when she gets on top she is pretty hard to deal with. I think her submission threat is just a little overrated, but she can easily overwhelm you if you let her get to a good spot. Her last fight was really pathetic, she gassed after 3 minutes and the way she nearly got ko’ed twice was crazy. This worries me a ton since she’s facing (imo) a better girl, but at the same time thye have very different skillsets. Mizuki is an NPC but she has a grappling background herself and a relatively well rounded skillset; Loma has improved her grappling but it’s still very underwhelming. I think it’s also worth noting their wins are about the same level; Loma is more experienced but when you look into it she’s really only beaten bottom tier girls; and imo, beating them less impressively than Amorim. At least Amorim is finishing them, Loma is dropping a round to almost everyone and is pretty thin margins as well. She is without a doubt the better striker here, and should this stay standing I expect her to maul Amorim on the feet. Amorim has some power and a freakihsly long reach but she can’t strike for ****. She has a terrible chin too, those reactions against Mizuki were extremely concerning to me. Loma doesn’t have any power but I expect those leg kicks to pay dividends throughout the fight. I don’t see Amorim having any striking success but I will say, her long reach and the td threat could defintely make Loma hesitant to throw, especially considering that she doesn’t separate well to begin with; losing a round to Brasil and Nunes in pure striking, when you’re supposed to be some super accomplished Thai striker, is a pretty bad look. It’s really difficult to back Amorim knowing that she has bad wrestling and is a guard puller, but I kind of think she will show levels on the mat. The biggest thing that stood out to me is Loma’s grappling; if you look at the stats she seems like she should cruise; she has a tdd of 69% and has gotten multiple tds of her own. However, her grappling is simply not good. She gets taken down in every single fight and worst of all, she forces grappling in every fight. I looked at the stats and she has attempted at least one takedown in EVERY single one of her UFC fights, even when facing grapplers like Thainara or Loopy. I think this is a really dumb idea here because Amorim can sub her off of her back or easily hit a reversal; the Gomes fight was a very bad look because of this. I expected Loma to grapple there since Gomes showed some really bad looks off of her back in regionals, and despite getting some control Loma was in hell there. She got reversed multiple times and put in some really bad sub attempts. She was putting herself in unnecessary danger all fight, and IMO I haven’t really seen improvements in this area. She still struggles off her back and is still forcing grappling in every fight despite still being a novice there. Amorim has a lot of bad habits with her grappling but I really think Loma is going to let her back into the fight here. She makes too many mistakes on the mat for me to back, and the fact she is shooting tds in every fight is another really bad look here.

Perez vs Sumudaerji
Sumudaerji DEC

Probably my favorite fight on the card here. I always love flyweights and Su is one of my guys. That losing streak he had was very bad but it’s also made him extremely underrated as a fighter; people just assume he’s trash and has no grappling but that’s not the case. He has rebounded nicely with three clean wins (raposo split made zero sense, clear UD) and is now getting his shot at the rankings. Perez is a very weird fighter to cap because he honestly doesn’t have a ton of holes anywhere, yet he’s extremely inconsistent. His level of comp compared to Su’s isn’t close, but he will have fights like the Mokaev one where he looks great against an elite guy, and then turn around and have fights like the Asu one, where he looks like a ghost of his former self (IK he won a round but watch that fight and you’ll see what I mean). I get why he’s the favorite but personally this line seems like clear recency bias; just because he ko’ed InnerG doesn’t mean Perez is back in good form. This is Perez’s first time being a favorite in 6 years, which makes sense given the level of comp but even then it’s weird to me when he is clearly the B side; they did not book this fight so Perez can continue his win streak. I think Su is being underrated yet again here. Obviously this is a big step up in comp and Su does have clear holes in his game, but I don’t think Perez can exploit it as easily as everyone is thinking. For starters, grappling. Obviously the concern in every Su fight is those gross, 6 losses by submission, but Perez isn’t a wrestler. He has subs on his record and will go for takedowns, but I don’t think he is some exceptional grappler. He has never came in with a wrestling heavy gameplan before and even if he does I really don’t see him being that effective. All anyone wants to do is focus on Su’s grappling so much that they completely ignore the strides he’s made since then. Su has great first layer tdd, made better by his lanky frame. He can be taken down still but he gets up to his feet well. We even saw some offensive improvements in the InnerG fight, so I know he’s been working hard there. Obviously I do expect Perez to take him down if he wants, but I really don’t think he’s going to dominate Su on the mat here; I know you can only improve so much when you already have a clear flaw in your game, but Perez is not some monster grappler or sub threat. The majority of his subs are all front chokes too, not RNC’s from the back (of which he only has 1). If Perez isn’t having success with takedowns, then I don’t know why he’s the favorite. I know, I know, the InnerG KO but don’t let that fight fool you, there has been a clear decline in Perez’s striking. Just go back to the Asu fight: Perez was throwing wild, looping hooks with poor set up, was literally walking into strikes all fight, and even got hurt twice with body kicks. Fighting all these grapplers made me forget that Perez is not some super advanced striker, and more importantly, he actually gets hit a LOT. Perez has good striking defense and keeps his hands high, but he also leaves a lot of opportunities to get hit. Even his KO wins like Nicolau/InnerG, Perez was still getting hit with some big shots; even after rocking InnerG with the left hook, Perez walked right into a front kick and a jab from a very hurt Charles. I think Su is going to be a very difficult puzzle to figure out. He has the longest reach in the division and knows how to use it very well. He also fights behind his kicks as well, making him even longer. Su doesn’t like to get hit and does panic a little when people turn fights into wars. Perez does pressure heavily and has frequent blitzes of hooks, but I don’t think he can be as reckless as usual here. Perez won’t be able to fight behind his jab and he will have to pressure to get the fight he wants. I think this will backfire on him because of Su’s reach; Su is a high level counter striker and I think he can frustrate Perez a lot here. I think this being in the big cage benefits Su even more, as it gives him more space to work; if this was in the apex I think Perez would have much more success. The other thing about Perez’s striking that I don’t like here is that he is mostly a boxer. He of course can kick but he mostly fights with his hands, and unless he can crash the pocket I think he is going to be whiffing on a lot and eating jabs for his troubles. I know he’s fought three cans but Su’s striking defense and distance management since the InnerG fight has been unreal; in the 9 rounds he’s fought, only 2 of them have his opponents landed more than 9 strikes. Perez does pressure a lot in his fights but I think he will be relegated to point fighting here due to the range. Su does have some durability issues so he could get clipped, but even then given his size I feel like he will miss the majority of the impact. If you ignore who he’s fighting and just look at purely Perez’s striking, it’s really not that special. He is predominantly a boxer and imo has declined noticeably on the feet. Again, I know he slept InnerG but he was still throwing those same sloppy hooks he was in the Asu fight; also worth noting since it’s the reason Perez is the favorite, InnerG is the most inconsistent fighter on the roster. Some days he looks unstoppable and others he looks like he’s never fought before. I also caution anyone with confidence in Perez, as he is a massive flake. He is being flown in as the B side, has a 20+ hour flight, struggles to make 125, and has durability/heart issues. If you give Perez the door he will take it, and his ability to find ways to get finished is just insane; even his two KO losses are pure memes, bro got ko’ed cold going for a takedown on Joe B. Su did not belong in the top 15 earlier in his career but he has learned from these errors. In an all striking match, I favor Su as the guy with more tools at his disposal. His striking defense, range management, and tools on the feet are really good, and I find it very hard to trust Perez at - money; why would you ever back a flake like him as a favorite?

Dias vs Lee
Dias SUB RD 2

I have so many questions about this fight: Why did they sign Sak Lee? Why is this trash the featured prelim over the local Chinese fighters? Why are they giving Dias a winnable fight? To me Dias is one of the worst guys ever signed off of dwcs. He was a part time fighter until last year and his tape is fraudulent. He literally sucks everywhere, has no real wins, 1 round of cardio, and is a quitter. I came into this one expecting to blindly fade him, but Lee is somehow even worse. I do love the randomness of these “local” signings (Leblanc, Johnston, etc.) but the problem is the UFC is signing the biggest jobbers available. Lee is a very confusing choice as he has no hype surrounding him, doesn’t train at one of the top gyms/managed by anyone good, isn’t Chinese, and doesn’t have a ufc level skillset either. He has no real wins to justify his record and got absolutely rinsed by the one dude with a pulse that he faced. I genuinely think the only reason he got signed is because Ali (Dias’s manager) asked them to find someone he could actually beat (much like his dwcs fight). At least with the last fight I can have a somewhat confident read since Ding has some actual skills, this fight is impossible to call since both guys are jobber level and both are bad at the same things. On the feet I guess I favor Dias, but I have no real confidence. Dias has some power but his striking is so clunky and limited. He only throws singular, looping shots to the head, and doesn’t have much else in his arsenal. He does hit kind of hard but he’s also insanely hittable and because of his limited, plodding game he walks into strikes all the time. Dias has terrible cardio too, so as a result he doesn’t throw very much either. Dias reacts so badly to being hit and even on dwcs he was getting touched up a good amount before the stoppage. Luckily for him though, Lee just may be an even worse striker. He only has one KO from standing, the rest at all gnps against jobbers. Dias has a wide and hittable stance but man, Lee’s defense is bad. He does not move his head ever and gets sniped on the feet any time his opponents try some offense. The Thani fight for example was just red flag after red flag. Every time Thani crashed the pocket he was rocking Lee’s head back, and he hasn’t shown any improvements since then. Dias is sloppy and hittable himself but I watch Lee’s fights and all I can think is how much of a liability he is. All Dias does is throw these slow, looping hooks with very limited footwork, but I don’t think Lee is good enough to pick up on that lol. If Lee comes out and blitzes Dias he could genuinely win, Dias hates getting hit and doesn’t have the cardio to keep up after r1. I haven’t really seen that aggression from Lee before though, so I can’t rely on it. Both of these guys are grapplers, really bad ones at that. However, this is the one area I feel like Dias has an advantage in; not a massive one, but he’s definitely better than Lee. Lee tries to be a grappler but he’s so bad at it. He is able to dominate his wins fairly easily, but he’s also only beating up complete cans. Dias of course doesn’t have any good winds either, but he definitely has faced better competition. The only person with a pulse Lee has fought is Agilan Thani, and he absolutely rinsed Lee is every aspect of MMA. Most concerning to me was how bad his tdd looked. Thani is the only guy who has actively tried to grapple Lee and he was scoring easy tds with no resistance. Lee would try some throws of his own and even had a cool back take at one point, but he would immediately fall off and get reversed. Once on his back he looked totally lost, and after that failed back take he immediately got put in an RNC and tapped. Dias’s grappling is really bad, and I would fade him against most in the ufc, but I think he is a better guy than Lee. Lee’s bjj is truly terrible, and he can’t wrestle at all. Dias has shown some awful looks himself in terms of tdd and grappling awareness, but he is a black belt and definitely more skilled than Lee. If Lee hits one of those weird scrambles and gets the back it could be interesting, if not though I expect him to get taken down and subbed at one point. I don’t really have a confident read on this one. I was expecting to just auto fade Lee but Dias is honestly just as bad as him. He looked horrible when he was an active fighter and only recently got back into MMA, so that’s a red flag. However as bad as he is, I simply don’t know why they signed Lee. Besides simply not being good, he has no hype and no marketability around him; I truly can’t understand why he got signed, he’s not even Chinese.

Ding vs Souza
Ding KO RD 3

This is such a random fight to throw together but I kind of love it; I think this is going to be a hilarious fight. Both of these guys are bad but they are both strikers with suspect defense, so I expect someone to go out here. Both of these guys had really bad showings on dwcs, but in different ways. I thought Ding’s fight was actually pretty close, his problem was that he couldn’t track Hamed down, who was running away the whole fight. That was not a good look but tbf that’s also not the type of style Souza is going to come with. He has relatively limited footwork and doesn’t use his size that well either. Souza’s dwcs fight was pretty bad, he had his moments but he got sniped by Kino****a all fight and ko’ed badly; a win that is aging really poorly. Besides getting ko’ed, Souza hasn’t really improved at all since then; he still shows the same flaws he did in the last fight. You can argue the same for Ding and at 31 he is likely not going to improve much, but I don’t think he is going to be as passive as his dwcs fight. Souza looks like the better guy on paper but he is a fraud imo, Ding is a bad fighter but I at least like some aspects of his game. Souza does not use his size at all. He pretty much only boxes with the occasional knee or leg kick mixed in, he has really bad tall man’s defense, and honestly a suspect chin too. Souza has been hurt before, after and on dwcs, and has never fixed his bad habit of leaning back to dodge strikes. He doesn’t recover that well either, Alex Silva probably could’ve finished him in r1 if he had any iq. I’ve seen Ding dropped many times as well and he too has tall man’s defense, but he actually has great recovery. He’s been sat down by power strikers like Nueraji and Huseynov, yet popped back up like nothing. I wouldn’t really say he has a bad chin, he’s just reckless. Despite how he looks, Souza doesn’t really hit that hard imo. He pretty much only uses his hands outside of that crazy last second KO on Alan Silva; the one time he used his size to his advantage. Ding is not a bad striker at all imo, just basic and reckless. He has a large frame himself and unlike Souza, he actually uses it. He throws lots of leg/body kicks, and all his punches are thrown straight down the middle. He pressures and forces a pretty high pace in most of his fights, and I don’t think Souza is going to be able to avoid the power shots very well. Because of his bad defensive habits and height, Souza really struggles up against the fence. I think this could be big for Ding because I really liked his clinch work against Huseynov; when he hurt him, Ding swarmed him against the fence and was ripping all sorts of knees and elbows. I don’t like how reckless Ding is but in this kind of fight I like it, because he has the durability while Souza does not. Souza could definitely catch him with something but he reacts really badly to being hit and is fighting someone who comes close to his size (he’s never faced that before). Ding will rush in and get hit but I think he can dish it out much better than Souza can take it. Ding’s record is padded with a lot of cans but he does have some real wins on there, Souza hasn’t fought anyone good in his career and has struggled against any of the real guys he’s fought. Despite his youth, he has been very inactive (suspended for roids) and hasn’t shown any improvements at all. Ding is not very good but I think he has a better striking skillset than Souza, more power, and is definitely more durable. I think this is going to be a really goofy fight where both guys get dropped, but I really think Souza is a fraud. There’s nothing impressive about his game and he sc****s by bad fighters really unimpressively.

Yadong vs Figuereido
Yadong KO RD 4

Why is Figgy taking this fight? He blamed a long flight as the reason he missed weight against Umar, and now he wants a 20 hour flight across Macau? Especially weird considering what happened the last time he was in Macau (Yan 50-44). Figgy has essentially been jobbing since that fight too, he knows he isn’t getting to the belt and physically he is a shell of himself. He looks so unbelievably slow, his fast-twitch speed is pretty much completely gone, his ability to take shots looks worse and worse, and he throws NOTHING on the feet. His last 4 performances have been devoid of any effort; if Montel showed up to do anything he probably would’ve won that fight as well. Being 38 at 135 is already not a good look as it is, but Figgy is pushing 50 in fight years. He had like 15 years of killing himself to make 125, and has had multiple 5 round wars. And now, he seemingly can’t even make 135 anymore. Obviously I expect him to make it this time but that cut definitely isn’t getting any easier. I said it in his last fight but Song has peaked imo. Despite his youth (although that’s debatable), I haven’t really seen any improvements in his game and he has fallen short every time he fights an elite of the division. He did way better than I was expecting against Sean, but I think a lot of that was also Sean being washed; once he woke up in r3 he smoked Song pretty badly. Ignoring Figgy’s outside factors, I think this is a complete layup for Song. Figgy throws nothing on the feet, doesn’t have a size advantage, doesn’t have a dynamic striking skillset (Song struggles heavily against rangy kickers/guys who fight behind their legs & reach), and I don’t think his wrestling is good enough anymore to try and hold Song down. The one area Song has improved a lot in is his wrestling, his tdd has looked very good ever since the Kyler fight. Figgy is still a really high level grappler but his control isn’t really that good and he will also do stupid **** like jumping for heel hooks. Song is also a big BW so I think the size difference will make it hard to get control as it is. On the feet I really don’t see a path to victory for Figgy. He doesn’t throw anything whatsoever, he literally feints more than he throws. Song is not going to get drawn into this boring affair like Montel did, and I think he is a far superior boxer to Figgy. Figgy is tough and his only ko loss was that injury to Cory, but his durability has declined a lot imo. He reacts so badly to being hit and even if he didn’t blow out his knee, Cory was beating the absolute **** out of him so the finish would've happened regardless. Song has had some stinkers on the feet like against Gutierrez/Sean but as previously mentioned, Song has always had a ton of issues with dynamic strikers. He has always been a boxer and struggles when you take the brawl away from him. I really don’t see Figgy having much for him on the feet, and if Song sets a pace from the jump he will break Figgy down. IMO, Figgy doesn’t have the cardio to do another 5 rounder, and he hasn’t really been pushed since the Cory fight; they’ve been two snoozefests where his opponents respect him too much to do anything. I would be really shocked if Song plays into Figgy’s game and tries to outpoint him. He can do that, but he easily has the ability to set a pace, get in Figgy’s face, and force a brawl. Obviously they’re different styles, but when he fought another former 125er in Cejudo, Song’s aggression and boxing looked the best it ever had. Figgy is very tough but I think Song is going to finish him late; I don’t trust Figgy’s cardio whatsoever, and I think he will look for the door once Song starts to land a lot. If it gets that far, I expect Figgy to massively slow down in the champ rounds. Maybe I am overrating Song’s finishing ability/Figgy’s lack of durability but he’s just looked like such a shell of himself lately. Given the lack of effort in his last two and the recent weight miss, I really think Figgy is done fighting. Other than another paycheck I really don’t get why he is taking this fight. He already knows the fight is going to be long and will affect his weight cut, he doesn’t have 5 hard rounds in him anymore, and his mileage is too high. I feel pretty confident that Song is going to find a finish here, I think this could potentially be the last Figgy fight we see.

Zhang vs Menifield
Zhang KO RD 1

Zhang’s last fight was incredibly disappointing but I think this is a perfect bounce back for him. Watching that fight back, he honestly didn’t look bad at all, it was the way it ended that was bad. I won’t even fault him for gassing since that was expected (imo) given his style, but the way he just gave up was so bad. Walker only threw like 5 kicks the entire fight and he somehow didn’t check any. Once compromised he just fell to the ground and quit; this was already bad enough but then he’s standing there after the fight grinning ear to ear and hugging Walker. Sportsmanship is fine and all but dude, why are you so happy after a quit job like that? I’m pretty worried we’ve seen his ceiling as well, it's gonna be really hard to see him going higher than top 10 with 1 round of cardio, bad durability, and that **** mentality. Zhang was marching him down bad and hurting Johnny with every shot, he actually looked like a menace early. However, all Johnny did was utilize basic footwork and it had Zhang completely lost on what to do. LHW top 15 is pretty trash but if you are struggling to cut the cage off against Walker of all people, I don’t see you lasting long. Despite these flaws, I really think Alonzo is a layup style for Zhang. He doesn’t wrestle, has no chin, terrible footwork/striking, and most of all, he is going to fight the exact fight Zhang wants. I’ve always thought Alonzo was an overachiever, his skillset is honestly pretty awful, he’s just a great athlete and hits hard. His striking is terrible and he has no real process, he just blitzes you with everything he’s got. Alonzo doesn’t tuck his chin or even really set things up, he just windmills his strikes and tries to kill you. He also doesn’t leg kick so Zhang should be fine. Zhang does have durability issues and since this will be a brawl he does have to be careful, but on a technical level I think he is leagues above Alonzo. I actually quite like Zhang’s striking. He has good leg kicks (although his ability to take them is not great lol), he throws his punches straight/doesn’t wind up, and has some really nasty elbows in the clinch. Unlike Alonzo, Zhang throws with accuracy and actually sets things up. Alonzo is going to bull rush him from the jump which could throw Zhang off, but at the same time he only needs one clean shot to sway the fight. Besides being super reckless and a bad technician, Alonzo has a terrible chin. He’s been put out 4 times and all of them brutal ones where he went out cold. Alonzo has been looking pretty washed recently as well; none of his losses are bad but they’ve all been wildly uncompetitve and his wins very unimpressive as well. He went life and death on the feet with harmless Walker (arguably lost that fight too), and then had one of the worst fights of 2025 against Giga fraud Oumar Sy, where he landed like 20 total strikes. Unless Zhang has PTSD from lastg fight and comes out timid, I think he should walk Alonzo down and brutally KO him. Zhang may be kind of fraudulent but he is genuinely a very good striker and extremely dangerous in r1. Alonzo doesn’t hold a technical advantage over him, won’t wrestle, and has a bad chin so I think this is a very favorable matchup. Zhang’s last fight was horrible but I really think Alonzo is a can. I expect him to smoke Alonzo easily.

Pavlovich vs Teixeira
Pavlovich KO RD 1

This fight doesn’t really make any sense but this is gonna be a r1 HW banger. Pav’s losing streak turned him into a boring, reserved point fighter but TBH he still looks good to me. Obviously it’s not fun to watch but these two fights showed me that Pav can be more than a R1 KO threat, and showed that he clearly still belongs in the top 5. Despite this reserved style, I think we see the old Pav here; no matter his approach, the style of Tallison is going to bring it out. We finally got to see what Talisson looked like past r1, and it was as bad as expected. He did fight smart with takedowns but considering how bad on the mat Tai is, it was very unimpressive. Outside of r1 he struggled a lot to get tds. He was also terrified to strike with Tai and was losing most of the striking until Tai decided to eat shots with his face. Worst of all though, Tai managed to outcardio him. Now, to be fair this was his first time outside of r1 but still; being more gassed than Tai and losing r3 is an astronomically bad look. Outside of a meme bonk in r1, I really don’t see how talisson wins this fight. Pav is better everywhere the fight goes, more experienced, and more proven against real competition. Even if he tries to be technical, Talisson is way too sloppy with bad tall man’s defense, and his aggressive style is going to force Pav to throw hands. I think brawls are better for Pav; he’s looked good (even if boring) in his last two but he’s also found himself getting hit too much because he overthinks things. If he just bites down on the mouthpiece and throws I think he will find the chin easily. Pav has more power, better striking, (somehow) a longer reach, better hardware, and better durability. Pav does walk into shots at times but he honestly has a titanium chin, Talisson… not so much. I don’t think Talisson is chinny per se, but he has really bad tall man’s defense and is very irresponsible in the pocket. He is going to need a KO 1 to win because he won’t be able to wrestle his way to a win here, nor win on points. Pav is hard to take down and a better wrestler than him, and he has better cardio too. I don’t like to factor it in since it usually never matters, but this is also a massive leap in competition for Talisson; he went life and death with jobber Tui and now gets the gatekeeper for the top 5. I think we see the old Pav here, I would be so shocked if this goes longer than 3 minutes.

Asakura vs Smotherman
Asakura KO RD 1

Please god don’t fumble this Kai. He has done irreversible damage to Rizin with his two UFC fights, but I think it goes without saying he’s better than that. The move to 135 should be great for him honestly, he was never a natural flyweight to begin with; prior to the UFC he had not made 125 since 2017. He was able to make the weight but imo it took a toll on his body and thusly his style; this was perfectly shown in the Elliot fight where Asakura simply just could not get going. Famous last words but this should be a layup for Kai. He’s facing a chinny, low iq, 100% boxer with a glass chin; if he loses this one he should retire from MMA. I’ve never liked Smotherman and I think he’s lucky to even be in the UFC. Weirdly enough, all three of his ufc fights have been highly competitive. That being said, he has high rolled his entire run thus far: Hadley is just a jobber and didn’t show up to win that fight, and the only reason the Simon/Sidey fights were close was because they were both weirdly terrified to strike with Cam. The Sidey one made especially no sense to me, as he almost never wrestles and wasn’t even in danger that entire fight. I find it highly unlikely Cam’s chin holds up but even if it does, he’s not even a good minute winner. He doesn’t have much power and doesn’t even really go for it in his wins; he just kind of light spars his way through everything. That’s why I don’t give him much credit for the Hadley win; sure, it was a great upset but Hadley didn’t show up to win. Cam didn’t do much to impress me there, literally all he did was stay active while Hadley stared & stared. Kai’s output hasn’t been great in the ufc but he’s also fought two grapplers, now he gets a pure striker who won’t so much as feint a takedown. Cam has better boxing on a technical level but I think Kai is a much better puncher. He also throws a lot of kicks which should help since Cam is heavy on the lead leg and doesn’t throw any kicks of his own. Kai also has great knees, especially to the body. These probably won’t be as effective since Cam doesn’t shoot, but he can also step into the pocket and just jam one up there if he wants. Kai also loves flying knees and I really don’t trust Cam to get out of the way. I am nervous backing Kai since he fumbled the Elliot fight so hard, but I would truly be shocked if he loses this one. Cam doesn’t shoot, only throws punches, has limited footwork, no defense, and no chin. I have a very hard time seeing this be anything but a KO 1 for Kai. At 135 I expect him to have more energy and I think he will blitz Cam for the early finish

Matthews vs Harris
Matthews KO RD 2

Ngl I didn’t feel like taping this one, seems like a fairly obvious win for Matthews. He should have Harris covered in all areas. I think Matthews can probably KO him, Harris has a really bad chin and the way he strikes he leaves himself so open to being hit. Matthews doesn’t really have power but his hand speed is super fast, and I feel like that could play a massive role here since Harris likes to get in the pocket and bang. I think Harris is actually a better grappler than Matthews but that shouldn’t matter since neither will wrestle. Even if Matthews tries, his offensive tds just aren’t good enough. Matthews isn’t much of a finisher but I think he can get the old man out of there.
